ai.description: *Sarada superba* is a 7–9 cm lizard with a brownish body and dark cross-bands. Males display a brilliant, multi-colored fan-throat with a central black patch and elongated, scale-covered throat flaps.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Sarada superba* is its exceptionally large, fan-like gular appendage, which is distinctively patterned with a bold, dark-edged blue patch.
ai.habitat: *Sarada superba* inhabits open, rocky plateaus and scrublands in the northern Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: During the breeding season, males perform vibrant displays by rapidly extending and retracting their colorful throat fans to attract mates and defend territories.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sarada superba* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sarada superba* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, primarily inhabiting high-elevation rocky plateaus above 800 meters.
